"Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 410 of 2024, under sections 419, 420, 506 of IPC P.S.- Kotwali Ayodhya, District- Ayodhya.

The contention of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is the marginal witness of an agreement entered into between the seller and purchaser whereas subsequently the registered sale deed has also been executed wherein the different marginal witnesses are there.

He added that the applicant is not involved in committing offence and even the purchaser had got ample opportunity to verify with respect to the integrity and the sanctity of the ownership of the seller.

He next added that identically situated co-accused, namely, Sujeet Yadav @ Sujeet Kumar Yadav has already been granted interim anticipatory bail in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No. 255 of 2024 vide order dated 20.12.2024 passed by this Court and applicant is seeking parity of the same.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No. 255 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Further submitted that the applicant has no previous criminal history and he is cooperating in the investigation proceedings.
He also submits that there is apprehension that the applicant will be arrested by the police thus, submission is that the the applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the complainant has opposed the contentions aforesaid and submits that the applicant is involved in committing the aforesaid offence, as such, he is not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail.
Learned AGA appearing for the State has also supported the contentions of the learned counsel for the complainant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Let notice be issued to opposite party no. 2, returnable at an early date.
Steps be taken within a week.
If steps are taken, office shall proceed accordingly.
List/put up this matter in fourth week of February, 2025.
In the meantime, the State as well as opposite party no. 2 may file their counter affidavits."
State counsel has failed to demonstrate from the counter affidavit that there is any adversarial fact which are pleaded in the bail application.
This Court finds that the applicant was enlarged on anticipatory bail after thorough considering the merits of the case.

The learned counsel for the State has also failed to submit any fact that the applicant is not cooperating with the investigation proceedings or otherwise any glaring fact which can adversely affect the merit of the case.
